Ollama integration glitch and feature request

The problem Hi, I'm running ollama server on a dedicated notebook, connected by HA for local assistant support. I use a custom thinking model with thinking disabled. I've observed that after performing consecutive operations multiple times, the voice assistant responds that it cannot find specific devices. For example, the command "Open the ceiling light in the living room area" results in the reply: "No ceiling light found in the living room area," while the command "Open the living room light" still works correctly, which is handled directly by the assist, not LLM. As mentioned in this discussion regarding `n_keep`, I suspect that the context limit is exceeded after multiple operations, causing parts of the prompt to be removed. This likely leads to the failure in recognizing certain devices. As far as I know, the model's thinking process also consumes context length. As referenced in this Home Assistant issue, if future versions (e.g., the upcoming 2025.7.1 release) implement hidden thinking instead of disabling it entirely, this issue may become more pronounced. Could we implement the following when configuring Ollama? - Display prompt length requirements based on entities exposed to Assist. - Provide an additional `n_keep` configuration option for manual adjustment. Feature request: Notify AI assistant when edits are rejected

Summary When using Zed's AI assistant integration (e.g., Claude Code), the assistant only receives feedback when I accept proposed edits. If I reject an edit, the assistant receives no notification. Current Behavior 1. Assistant proposes a file edit 2. I click "Reject" (or "Reject All") 3. The edit is discarded 4. The assistant has no idea I rejected it - it assumes the edit went through or has to re-read the file to discover it wasn't applied Desired Behavior When I reject an edit, the assistant should receive feedback indicating: - The edit was rejected - Optionally: which file/edit was rejected This allows the assistant to: - Understand something was wrong with the proposed change - Ask what needs to be different - Avoid repeating the same mistake Use Case I was working with the assistant on image thumbnails. It proposed an edit with black borders where I needed white. I rejected it, but the assistant didn't know - I had to manually tell it "I rejected that, try again with white instead." With rejection feedback, the assistant could immediately ask "I see you rejected the edit - what should I change?" Related This pairs well with the UX improvement in #48128 (renaming Keep All to Accept All) - both are about clearer communication in the edit review flow.

Feature Request Is your feature request related to a problem? In VS Code, I can select and copy formatted text from the Markdown preview pane and paste it into other apps (Slack, Notion, Google Docs) with formatting preserved. This doesn't work in Zed's markdown preview. Describe the solution you'd like Allow selecting and copying rendered/formatted text from the Markdown preview, preserving rich text formatting (headers, bold, links, tables, etc.) when pasting into other applications. Describe alternatives you've considered - Exporting to HTML and copying from browser - Using external markdown preview tools Additional context This is a common workflow for documentation writers who draft in Markdown but share formatted content via Slack/email/docs.

Feature Request: Unified Git Changes Tree (like VS Code/Cursor) Summary The Git Changes panel currently separates files into "Tracked" and "Untracked" sections. This differs from VS Code/Cursor behavior where all changes appear in a single unified tree with inline status indicators. Since many Zed users come from VS Code/Cursor, aligning with this familiar UX pattern would improve the experience. Current Behavior Zed's Git Changes panel splits files into two separate sections: - **Tracked** — Modified and deleted files - **Untracked** — New files This separation forces users to scan two different areas to understand the full scope of their changes. Proposed Behavior Display all changed files in a **single unified tree** organized by directory structure, with inline status indicators for each file: - `M` — Modified - `U` — Untracked/New - `D` — Deleted - `A` — Added (staged) Files should appear in their natural directory location regardless of their git status. Why This Matters 1. **Familiar mental model** — Most Zed users come from VS Code/Cursor and expect a unified changes view 2. **Easier to scan** — One tree to review instead of two separate sections 3. **Better context** — Seeing new and modified files together in their directory structure shows the full picture of changes 4. **Reduced cognitive load** — No need to mentally merge two lists when planning a commit Visual Comparison VS Code (unified tree) ✅ Zed (split view) ❌ --- Happy to provide more context if helpful. Feature Request: File Explorer Sorting Options in Settings

Summary Request for configurable file and folder sorting options in the Zed file explorer through `settings.json`. Motivation While macOS users benefit from alphabetical sorting by default, it would be valuable to have explicit control over file explorer sorting behavior across all platforms. This would provide: 1. **Consistency**: Ensure predictable sorting behavior regardless of platform 2. **Customization**: Allow users to choose their preferred sorting method 3. **Documentation**: Make sorting behavior explicit and discoverable Proposed Solution Add file explorer sorting configuration to `settings.json` under the `project_panel` section: [code omitted] Possible Sorting Methods - **alphabetical**: Sort by name (case-insensitive) - **modified**: Sort by last modified date - **size**: Sort by file size - **type**: Sort by file extension/type Additional Context - Currently, sorting appears to work alphabetically on macOS by default - This feature would complement existing project panel settings - VSCode has similar functionality with `explorer.sortOrder` Implementation Notes Could be implemented as: 1. Extension of existing `project_panel` settings 2. Similar to how `git_status`, `file_icons`, etc. are currently configured 3. Would maintain backward compatibility with current default behavior Would you be interested in this feature? I'd be happy to help with implementation if this aligns with Zed's roadmap.

Feature Request: Show Tool Call Input Arguments Before Approval in Agent Chat

Summary When using Zed's agent panel, tool calls suggested by the LLM should display their input arguments/parameters before the user approves or declines them. Currently, only the tool name and results are visible, but not the arguments that will be passed to the tool. **This should apply to both:** - **Native Zed tools** (edit_file, terminal, read_file, grep, list_directory, etc.) - **Custom MCP tools** (Model Context Protocol tools added by users via context servers) Motivation **The Problem:** Users cannot see what data the agent intends to use when invoking tools. This creates a transparency gap where approval decisions are made without knowing: - What file will be edited and how - What command will be executed in the terminal - What paths will be searched or modified - What content will be read or written - **What arguments are being passed to custom MCP tools** **Why This Matters:** 1. **Transparency** — Users should understand what actions will be performed before approving them 2. **Safety** — Prevents accidental execution with incorrect or dangerous parameters 3. **Trust** — Builds confidence in AI agent interactions by showing all details upfront 4. **Learning** — Helps users understand the agent's reasoning and tool usage patterns 5. **Debugging** — Makes it easier to identify when the agent misunderstands requirements 6. **MCP Tool Trust** — Especially important for custom/third-party MCP tools where behavior may be less predictable Current vs. Desired Behavior **Current Behavior:** [code omitted] **Desired Behavior:** [code omitted] **Example with Custom MCP T

What problem does this feature solve? 同时使用 v-if 和 v-for 时，在Vue2中 v-for 的优先级是比 v-if 优先级更高的，但在 vue3 中变成了 v-if 比 v-for 的优先级更高，所以我想是否可以通过编辑时的静态代码分析动态决定 v-if 和 v-for 的优先级。 如： 1. <div v-for="(value, key, index) in list" v-if="value.size === 20"></div> 2. <div v-for="(value, key, index) in list" v-if="user.age > 20"></div> 在例 1 中，v-if 使用了 v-for 声明的变量 value，就将这里编译成 v-for 比 v-if 优先级更高； 在里 2 中，v-if 只用到了 v-for 之外的变量，这里就编译成 v-if 比 v-for 的优先级更高； 其他情况，如 this 里也出现了 v-for 声明的变量 value，肯定是局部作用域优先，用到的仍然是 v-for 声明的。 What does the proposed API look like? 1. <div v-for="(value, key, index) in list" v-if="value.size === 20"></div> 2. <div v-for="(value, key, index) in list" v-if="user.age > 20"></div>
